memory_update.text: CHEF should be retained for Layer 2 as a high-priority underfollowed restaurant supply-chain candidate because it explicitly maps to center-of-the-plate beef, seafood, and poultry distribution rather than only generic foodservice distribution.

SEB is an underfollowed embedded-protein candidate: pork exposure is real, but restaurant-specific sensitivity may be diluted by the parent company's diversified businesses, export exposure, and hog-cycle economics.

HFFG is a speculative shadow candidate below the preferred market-cap threshold; keep only if official filings confirm restaurant customer concentration, meaningful meat/poultry/seafood mix, and acceptable liquidity/governance risk.

The node should include both processors and distributors: custom-cut meat, seafood processing, prepared proteins, and specialty distributor logistics may be closer to restaurant menu execution than commodity packer volume alone.

Need a later pass for private or non-US suppliers that are important customer dependencies, such as Mistica Foods, Cargill Protein, National DCP, and other chain-specific procurement organizations, because they may explain which public companies are only partial proxies.

summary: Expanded the center-of-plate protein sourcing node with one reference protein processor and three underfollowed or shadow candidates. The strongest underfollowed mapping is not only upstream animal protein processing, but also specialty distribution and custom-cut protein logistics where restaurant execution depends on consistent SKU availability, portioning, seafood/meat handling, and chain/independent customer coverage. Commodity protein cycles remain the main falsification risk: later layers should separate true value-added foodservice exposure from simple beef, pork, chicken, egg, or seafood price leverage.
